articles.title: Matthew Rhys' sister 'so proud of him' after historic Emmy wins
articles.summary: Rhys, from Cardiff, became the first person to win two lead acting Emmy prizes in one night.
body: The sister of Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys said her family had been "pinching ourselves all week" following his historic Emmy success.

His older sister Rachel Evans, who accompanied Rhys to the ceremony in Los Angeles, said she was starstruck seeing Hollywood royalty at the event, and revealed that she and her brother called their parents afterwards, who were sat at home in their dressing gowns.
Speaking to Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales, Evans said watching Rhys win the awards was "an experience I will never ever forget or probably match".
She said that as the "bossy" older sister, she told him that morning that he needed to prepare, adding: "If you win, you cannot wing it."

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo Tells Rob Bonta ‘Don’t You Dare’ Settle the Antitrust Lawsuit Against Paramount: ‘Do Not Cave’
articles.summary: Mark Ruffalo is encouraging California attorney general Rob Bonta and his coalition of 11 other state AGs not to settle their lawsuit against Paramount Skydance and keep David Ellison from acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery. “Don’t you dare, [Rob Bonta], do not cave,” Ruffalo wrote on X.
body: Paramount Skydance’s $111 billion deal for Warner Bros. was approved by the Department of Justice in June. However, the deal was put on hold thanks to the antitrust lawsuit from Bonta and his team of state AGs. The Wall Street Journal, citing anonymous sources, reported Friday that Paramount Skydance and Bonta are in “advanced talks” to reach a settlement.

Ruffalo isn’t the only one asking Bonta to hold his ground. Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts wrote on Facebook Saturday morning that President Donald Trump banning CNN from the White House is a warning of things to come if Paramount Skydance swallows Warner Bros. (Trump also banned MSNOW and Politico).

“As Trump tries to ban CNN from the White House, it would be a massive mistake to cave on the Paramount merger,” Warren wrote. “The last thing we need is another Trump-controlled media conglomerate abusing its power to stomp out competition. This is a dangerous merger.”

articles.title: Ed Sheeran admits 'mistakes' at first show since Macklemore controversy
articles.summary: The singer spoke about Israel and Gaza after Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage.
body: The singer began his concert in Philadelphia by addressing the controversy that has since engulfed the tour and prompted all of his support acts to quit.

"I never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about free speech and the most complex political issue on the planet," Sheeran said.
He described the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attacks as "horrific" and called the situation in Gaza "unjustifiable".
The singer has said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoters, not him. The row has seen ticket prices drop and sales decline for the remaining US leg of his Loop Tour.

articles.title: ‘Ride or Die’ Canceled by Prime Video After One Season
articles.summary: “Ride or Die” has been canceled by Prime Video after one season, Variety can confirm. The streamer’s Hannah Waddingham and Octavia Spencer-led buddy dramedy premiered in July of this year. It was first reported that Spencer and Waddingham were teaming up for the series in December 2023.
body: In her review of Season 1, Variety ’s Aramide Tinubu wrote that “‘Ride or Die’ works best when it fully leans into the ‘Thelma & Louise’ aspects of the central storyline… Spencer and Waddingham have a robust and genuine chemistry — a companionship that will undoubtedly resonate with countless viewers. Moreover, watching Waddingham as a full-fledged action star is something everyone should be witnessing on a daily basis.”
Other cast members included Ed Skrein, Calam Lynch, Savannah Steyn, Jamie Parker, and Jacky Ido, with Sylvia Hoeks and Bill Nighy.

Tessa Coates created the series and serves as executive producer and showrunner along with Matt Miller and director Peyton Reed. The show is produced by Paramount Television Studios, Amazon MGM Studios as well as Andy and Barbara Muschietti’s Double Dream and Octavia Spencer ’s Orit Entertainment. Coates, Miller, and Reed executive produce alongside Spencer for Orit Entertainment; Waddingham; Andy Muschietti, Barbara Muschietti, and Irene Yeung for Double Dream; Brian Clisham; and Stephanie Kluft.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran Addresses Macklemore Controversy While on Stage at First Concert Since Rapper Dropped From Tour: ‘What Is Happening in Gaza Is Catastrophic and Unjustifiable’
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran addressed the controversy surrounding Macklemore’s removal from his Loop Tour on Saturday night, speaking from the stage at Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field during his first concert since the rapper was dropped from the trek.
body: “I just wanna say before they come on stage [that] they said yes to being on stage with the knowledge that the world thought I was a certain type of person,” he continued. “They said yes with the knowledge that the world may hate them too for standing on stage with me and I am so grateful for them being on stage tonight and standing on stage with me in front of you guys.”

The controversy also prompted Sheeran to scrap the B stage — a smaller secondary platform closer to the crowd where he typically performs several songs — because he “was scared of what might happen if [he] stood in the middle.”

“I’m gonna be totally honest with you, I didn’t know what this audience would be like tonight,” he said on stage. “I didn’t know if I would have things thrown at me. I didn’t know if people would be angry at me.”

Saturday’s concert marked Sheeran’s first performance since a tumultuous week for the U.S. leg of his Loop Tour, which saw Macklemore removed from the remaining dates following the rapper’s onstage remarks in support of Palestinians during Sheeran’s Sept. 4 and 5 shows at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

articles.title: Everything we know about the Ed Sheeran and Macklemore controversy
articles.summary: The show in Philadelphia comes after rapper Macklemore was dropped from Ed Sheeran's tour over pro-Palestinian comments.
body: British singer Ed Sheeran has performed his first show since facing backlash over a controversial decision to drop rapper Macklemore from his tour.
The decision - which Sheeran said was made by his promoter, not by himself - stemmed from pro-Palestinian comments Macklemore made on stage earlier this month.
Sheeran addressed the controversy and spoke for nearly four minutes at the start of his set in Philadelphia on Saturday, saying he had made "mistakes" handling the fallout.

"I have tried in my career not to be a political commentator of any kind, because I want my music and shows to be about unity, not division; about humanity, not politics. But this is a humanitarian issue, and I cannot hide how I feel about it anymore."

articles.title: Why Are So Many Star Trek Admirals Evil? An Investigation
articles.summary: If you encounter an admiral in the Star Trek universe, chances are they're going to be up to something shady. But why does that happen so frequently?
body: Welcome to Trekspertise, a series where we break down the technology, history, details, and decisions that make the Star Trek universe so complex — and so fun.

On all the "Star Trek" shows, Starfleet captains are typically depicted as stalwart, capable, principled leaders, possessed of uncanny talents and ineffable insight that allows them to make important command decisions in an instant, often while under extreme pressure. Each captain has their unique command style, of course — Kirk is judicious yet passionate, Picard is measured and aloof, Sisko is angry and willing to flout rules, Janeway is caring and authoritarian — but they all wield their management duties with grace and aplomb.

Bad admirals are a widespread phenomenon on "Star Trek" to the point of becoming a cliche. Which leads one to ask: What happens to Starfleet captains that make them turn to the dark side once they get promoted? Why are so many admirals bad?

articles.title: Sex and dating for the sandwich generation - Sharon Horgan on her latest comedy Youth
articles.summary: "It's really weird watching yourself age on screen because that's not fun," Horgan reveals.
body: Casual sex. Relationships. Parenting. Sharon Horgan has already seen us through several life stages via hit comedy dramas such as Pulling, Catastrophe and Motherland.
Now, with her latest show Youth, Horgan puts the spotlight on 50-something women, imbued with her trademark tightly balanced mix of hilarity and pathos.

The HBO Max series sees Horgan's character, Alex, gamely attempting to juggle a stressful publishing career while looking after a teenage son and elderly parents. She's part of the so-called sandwich generation, those in midlife who have to juggle caring responsibilities for old and young while often working, too.
And that's not all - Alex is also back in the dating game following a divorce.

articles.title: Ruby Rose Remembers Hayden Panettiere: “We Had Everything in Common”
articles.summary: "All that she ever wanted was to have her story told her way, on her terms," the 'Orange Is the New Black' star said of the 'Heroes' actress.
body: Panettiere, the Heroes and Nashville actress, died on Aug. 16 at 36 years old.
The Orange Is the New Black star got choked up when asked by Entertainment Tonight how she hopes Panettiere is remembered during the premiere of Fox’s Special Forces.
“That was my best friend,” she said of Panettiere. “We spoke everyday for five years.”

“I saw her, she saw me, and I just remember thinking, ‘Oh, no.’ And then she ran up anyway and was like, ‘Hey, I’m Hayden. Can we go talk somewhere? We’ve got a lot in common.’ And I just laughed. I was like, ‘What?’” Rose recalled. “She says I said, ‘I don’t think so,’ but I think I just laughed. And then we went and talked, and we had everything in common.”

articles.title: ‘The Traitors’ Cast: Kristin Chenoweth, Chloe Kim, Rashad Jennings, Whitney Leavitt and More Join Peacock Hit
articles.summary: The reality television hit, which was just renewed for three additional seasons, is set to return in 2027.
body: The Traitors ‘ next celebrity season is set to be released in 2027, and Peacock has unveiled its star-studded cast.

Musical theater icon Kristin Chenoweth, Olympic gold medalist Chloe Kim, The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives Leavitt and former NFL player Rashad Jennings are among the upcoming season. The next season will feature much more Hollywood talent, including several actors, than normal. There’s also plenty of love for the Bravo-universe this season, although that’s no surprise.

The Traitors — based on a Dutch format — is a competition where contestants are split into two categories: Faithfuls and Traitors. All 23 contestants will start as Faithfuls before Cumming decides which (typically) three players will become Traitors. The titular role then works to sneak past the rule-following players who are attempting to figure out who the Traitors are while choosing a Faithful player each night to “murder.” Studio Lambert produces the series, which utilizes reality TV stars and other media personalities for its contestant pool.
